original_value: Bioinformatics and biophysical studies of intrinsically disordered proteins and regions (IDRs) note the high entropy at individual sequence positions and in conformations sampled in solution. This prevents application of the canonical sequence-structure-function paradigm to IDRs and motivates the development of new methods to extract information from IDR sequences. We argue that the information in IDR sequences cannot be fully revealed through positional conservation, which largely measures stable structural contacts and interaction motifs. Instead, considerations of evolutionary conservation of molecular features can reveal the full extent of information in IDRs. Experimental quantification of the large conformational entropy of IDRs is challenging but can be approximated through the extent of conformational sampling measured by a combination of NMR spectroscopy and lower-resolution structural biology techniques, which can be further interpreted with simulations. Conformational entropy and other biophysical features can be modulated by post-translational modifications that provide functional advantages to IDRs by tuning their energy landscapes and enabling a variety of functional interactions and modes of regulation. The diverse mosaic of functional states of IDRs and their conformational features within complexes demands novel metrics of information, which will reflect the complicated sequence-conformational ensemble-function relationship of IDRs.

result.paraphrase: Bioinformatics and biophysical analyses of intrinsically disordered proteins and regions (IDRs) emphasize the high entropy at individual sequence positions and among the conformations sampled in solution. As a result, the canonical sequence-structure-function paradigm does not apply well to IDRs, creating a need for new methods to extract information from IDR sequences. We contend that IDR sequence information cannot be fully captured by positional conservation alone, because this mainly reflects stable structural contacts and interaction motifs. Instead, evolutionary conservation of molecular features can disclose the full breadth of information encoded in IDRs. Measuring the large conformational entropy of IDRs experimentally is difficult, but it can be approximated by the extent of conformational sampling assessed using a combination of NMR spectroscopy and lower-resolution structural biology methods, and then interpreted with simulations. Conformational entropy and other biophysical properties can be altered by post-translational modifications, which give IDRs functional advantages by tuning their energy landscapes and enabling diverse functional interactions and regulatory modes. The varied mosaic of IDR functional states and conformational features within complexes calls for new metrics of information that capture the intricate sequence-conformation ensemble-function relationship of IDRs.
